checklist_item: Inference on beta of n = k*d^beta (g0401-g0502 section B)
claim_as_stated: A $1m+ line holds about one grant; under beta = 1 a $1m line would hold about 200 grants at a $5k average, so beta near 1 is ruled out; the evidence favours the low-beta end.
exact_values_found: Validator fit of n_i = max(1, k*d_i^beta), equal-size grants within a line, Sum n = 77,364, JCF FY2023 lines plus 6,260 unitemised recipients sharing $49.6m: predicted grants under $50k / $50k-$1m / over $1m = 75,444 / 1,832 / 88 at beta 0; 79 over $1m at beta 0.2; 108 at beta 0.3; 0 at beta 0.35 and above; 77,364 / 0 / 0 at beta 0.75 and 1. Published 75,380 / 1,908 / 76. Without unitemised recipients: best at beta 0.1 (77 over $1m), 0 over $1m from beta 0.3.
discrepancies: The doc argument is right within the model, but the stated reason (one line holds one grant) is not what the data show.
contradictory_evidence: g0401-g0502 B5 already found the model gives 0 lines of mean grant $1m+ for beta >= 0.40 at Fidelity.
interpretation_challenge: beta near 1 is ruled out only within the model equal-size-per-line assumption; a line can mix one large grant with many small ones. On that model the evidence points to beta of about 0-0.3, so the pooled broad per-grant share is about 28-31% (31.2% at beta 0, 29.6% at 0.25), not the 17-31% range. The core share (7-8.5%) is unaffected. One single-issue sponsor-year is the basis.
